Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

liability noun

legal responsibility

also liable, be liable for, legally responsible, answerable, be held responsible, accountable

classical

Cic. Fam. 6.1.4: ut nihil in vītā nōbīs praestandum praeter culpam putēmus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 6.3.5: quem tamen ego praestāre nōn poteram (Lewis & Short)

praestō, praestāre, praestitī, praestitum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

answer for, be responsible for

To vouch for, warrant, take upon oneself: to be liable for a loss is damnum praestāre. Its other common senses are to excel, to show, and to perform (see perform).

Other words

  • obnoxius, obnoxia, obnoxium — liable, answerable (to a penalty, a law, a person)

    adjective, with the dative, declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Truc. 4.3.61: ego tibi mē obnoxium esse fateor culpae compotem (Lewis & Short); Dig. 11.3.14: ego lēge Aquīliā obnoxius sum (Lewis & Short)

    Subject to punishment, liable; then subject, submissive, beholden in general. It never means “obnoxious”.

Examples

  • simus eā mente ut nihil in vītā nōbīs praestandum praeter culpam putēmus

    let us be of a mind to think that in life we must answer for nothing but our own wrongdoingCic. Fam. 6.1.4 (Lewis & Short)

See also debt, undertake responsibility, guarantee.
